title: gator-runtime-pin-v1
description: The committed record of which shipped Gator runtime is in force in a governed repo (.gator/runtime-pin.json). Repo-side half of the runtime split (roadmap item 19, Variant A): the manifest proves from git history alone which exact runtime bytes governed each commit, while the runtime executes from the installed CLI. Emitted by gator-update and gatorize after a successful overlay (Phase 1); read by the runtime resolver from Phase 2 onward. Additive-friendly per the contracts-layer invariant: additionalProperties stays true; removing or renaming a required field is a version bump (new file, new title, one-cycle coexistence).

schema.description: Schema tag. Readers MUST check this before interpreting other fields.

runtime_version.description: The Gator CLI version whose shipped runtime is in force (e.g. '2.9.0'). Under Variant A fail-closed semantics (Phase 2+), an installed CLI older than this version refuses to run governance for the repo.

pinned_at.description: UTC timestamp of pin emission (ISO 8601, seconds precision, Z suffix).

pinned_by_machine.description: Machine id (~/.gator/machine-id `id:` field) of the machine that emitted the pin, or null when unavailable. Informational — not part of the integrity proof.

manifest.description: sha256 of every file in the shipped runtime in force, keyed by posix path relative to the shipped scripts dir (.includes/scripts/ on v2, scripts/ on v1). __pycache__ excluded. This is the integrity half of the trust-boundary requirement: history proves WHICH bytes; availability of those bytes is external (installed wheel / mirror). An empty object is legal only for post-Phase-4 repos that no longer carry repo-resident runtime.
